title: Certificate rotation race in private control plane causes transient RBAC denial and dropped audit events
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-03-09 we received multiple escalations from two private deployment customers reporting short-lived 403s for inference requests and gaps in audit streams during a scheduled certificate rotation window. Investigation shows a race between control-plane certificate chain rotation and the private agent's KMS envelope key rotation. The race caused rolebinding lookups to fallback to cached membership that evaluated to false for a small percentage of requests and simultaneously queued audit events that failed to be encrypted/dequeued resulting in missing audit records for ~6-12 minutes.
impact_details: Affected surface: Private (VPC/on-prem) control planes running agent v1.12.1-1.12.2 with automated cert rotation enabled. Two customers reported user-facing 403s (authz failures) for ~3-9 minutes during rotation. Audit ingestion lag caused ~1.2k audit events to be dropped or delayed beyond retention window for one customer that had strict compliance ingestion. Root cause thread race between cert hot-swap path and KMS envelope key TTL renewal where the control plane temporarily presented a certed identity that the agent's RBAC cache invalidated, triggering expensive KMS decrypt retries that exhausted the async audit buffer.
reproduction_steps:
1) Deploy private control plane and agent v1.12.2 with auto-rotate enabled and KMS envelope rotation scheduled at 03:00 UTC.
2) Initiate cert rotation (simulate immediate chain replacement).
3) Force heavy auth traffic (100 RPS) and watch for RBAC evaluation hits that miss due to short-lived identity mismatch.
4) Observe audit queue metrics and KMS decrypt error spikes in the agent logs.
Expected: no 403s and reliable audit delivery. Observed: transient 403s and audit gaps.
root_cause: Two concurrent operations (cert chain hot-swap + KMS envelope rotation) were not serialized. When the control plane rotated certs it briefly served a newly-signed certificate chain before the agent completed KMS envelope refresh; the agent invalidated local RBAC caches and attempted KMS decrypts against a partially rotated envelope metadata set leading to a spike in decrypt failures and audit buffer overflows. The code path lacked defensive retries with exponential backoff and did not persist audit events to a durable store if KMS temporarily rejected decrypt requests.
short_term_mitigation:
1) Immediately disabled automated cert rotation for impacted customers via control-plane feature flag (rolled between 2026-03-09 23:40 UTC and 2026-03-10 00:05 UTC).
2) Applied configuration change to increase agent audit buffer and enable synchronous fallback write to disk for audit events for customers with strict compliance.
3) Contacted affected customers with timeline and requested they extend rotation window while we deploy a hotfix.
remediation_plan:
1) Backport patch to private-agent that serializes cert rotation and KMS envelope refresh (agent v1.12.3). Patch includes: serialized rotation lock, robust KMS decrypt retry with jitter and capped exponential backoff, audit persistence to ephemeral on-disk queue as fallback.
2) Add guard in control-plane to publish rotation-ready signal after confirming agents report successful envelope update.
3) Add end-to-end test for concurrent rotation scenarios and KMS error injection.
4) Ship rollout with canary to two low-impact customers, monitor for 24 hours, then progressive rollout to remaining customers.
rollback_plan: If v1.12.3 causes regressions: revert feature flag to disable serialized rotation and revert agent to v1.12.2 while re-enabling previous mitigations (increased audit buffer + disk fallback). Control-plane will be set to manual rotation until remediation is verified.
qa_steps: Unit tests covering rotation lock and retry behavior
Integration test in staging with KMS error injection to validate audit persistence
Canary deployment to two private customers (non-production) and monitor auth 403 rate, audit delivery, KMS error rate
Load test at production-like 200 RPS during rotation window to confirm no auth failures
rollout_timeline: 2026-03-12: hotfix branch and internal review. 2026-03-13: security review and canary build creation. 2026-03-14: deploy canary to Customer A and Customer B during off-peak. 2026-03-15 to 2026-03-16: monitor and progressive rollouts. 2026-03-18: target completion for all customers.
customer_communications: Customer A (FinData Labs): incident call held 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC; follow-up email with mitigation steps sent. Customer B (LedgerHouse): SLA credit offered; engineering review scheduled. Compliance contact for Customer B requested signed attestation once audit delivery is confirmed.
